This `-2` is the last legacy-form mint.

Goals.Goal: **The mint — `ngrace spec new`.** The verb takes a human slug and mints `C-<SLUG>-<N>-<HASH>` where `<N>` is the lineage (`-1` for a first mint) and `<HASH>` is the first **8** characters of the uppercase hex SHA-256 of the UTF-8 bytes `<branch>\n<canonicalTimestamp>`. The timestamp comes from `--timestamp` or `NGRACE_SPEC_TIMESTAMP` (flag wins) and is refused when absent or not parseable as ISO 8601; the branch comes from `--branch`, `NGRACE_SPEC_BRANCH`, or `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`, and is refused when none resolves. The verb never reads the wall clock. `--supersedes <C-PRED>` derives the slug and `<N>` from the predecessor's parsed directory name instead of `-1`. On success it writes the skeleton and prints three lines — the relative spec path, the resolved `mint:` line, and the `mint-search:` line naming the prior active/archive bundle counts for the slug — so the searched-before-minting statement's collision half is the tool's and its scope half stays the author's.

**The refusals.** `spec new` refuses, each with a message naming the offending value and the reason: an argument that is a hand-typed id (any positional beginning `C-`, with or without a suffix — the suffix is the tool's to mint); a slug whose final token is all digits (ambiguous with lineage); an input already carrying the minted `-<N>-<HASH>` suffix; an absent or invalid timestamp; an unresolved branch; an unparseable `--supersedes` predecessor; and a resolved id whose directory already exists under `active/` or `archive/`. Refusal writes nothing — no directory, no file.

**The lineage — `ngrace supersede`.** A shared `parseBundleId` reads a directory name into `{ slug, lineage, hash, minted }`: a minted id strips `-<HASH>` then `-<N>`; a legacy hash-less id with a trailing `-<digits>` yields that lineage; any other legacy id yields no lineage. The successor's lineage is `(lineage ?? 1) + 1` and its slug is unchanged, so legacy `C-FOO` → `C-FOO-2-<HASH>` and legacy `C-FOO-2` → `C-FOO-3-<HASH>`. `supersede`'s `--replacement` becomes optional: when given it must exist and be exactly that successor (same slug, next lineage), refusing any other directory; when omitted, the verb mints the successor through the same routine (taking the mint's timestamp/branch inputs) before writing `superseded` and moving the predecessor. A hash-less successor is accepted only when it already exists, never newly minted.

**The anchor grammar, and the legacy edge.** `ANCHOR_PATTERNS.change` stays `/^C-[A-Z0-9]+(?:-[A-Z0-9]+)*$/` — unchanged — so every consumer keeps accepting the legacy corpus. `src/artifact/types.ts` gains `ANCHOR_PATTERNS.mintedChange` `/^C-[A-Z0-9]+(?:-[A-Z0-9]+)*-[1-9][0-9]*-[0-9A-F]{8}$/`, the `parseBundleId` parser, and a `nextBundleLineage` helper. The minted pattern is **not** added to `ANCHOR_FAMILIES`: the `change` family's prefix classification already owns `C-`, and a second `C-` family would classify every legacy hash-less id as malformed (`ANCHOR_FAMILIES` and `classifySemanticAnchorTag` live in `src/artifact/grammar.ts` at `:247` and `:352`; the minted pattern and the parser live in `src/artifact/types.ts`, and `grammar.ts` is untouched). `docs/schema-reference.md` is consequently byte-identical (no registered shape inventory changes); it is proven by the byte-invariance criterion, not regenerated.

**`F249`'s product half — the seed.** `renderChangeSpec`'s `NonGoals` section carries a docs-and-examples placeholder naming both `README.md` and `examples/` and instructing the author to replace it, so a freshly minted skeleton passes `checkDocsAndExamplesDecision` and a bare mint is no longer CI-red. The exemption alternative — exempting a skeleton still at `AC-SKELETON` in `check-teaching-surface` — is **not** taken; the seed is data the author can see and must replace, where an exemption weakens a shipped guard. `check-teaching-surface` and its predicate are unchanged.

**The mint contract, pinned.** `ngrace spec new` takes exactly one of the positional `<SLUG>` or `--supersedes <C-PRED>`: `ngrace spec new <SLUG> --timestamp <ISO8601> [--branch <name>] [--path <root>]` and `ngrace spec new --supersedes <C-PRED> --timestamp <ISO8601> [--branch <name>] [--path <root>]`. `<SLUG>` matches `^[A-Z0-9]+(?:-[A-Z0-9]+)*$` and does not carry the `C-` prefix; the tool prepends it. `<N>` is `1`, or the predecessor's parsed lineage plus one. `<HASH>` is `createHash("sha256").update(\`${branch}\n${canonicalTimestamp}\`).digest("hex").toUpperCase().slice(0, 8)` — **8** characters, the `short` of `D38`. `canonicalTimestamp` is `new Date(input).toISOString()`, refused when `Number.isNaN(Date.parse(input))`; input is `--timestamp` or `NGRACE_SPEC_TIMESTAMP`, flag wins. `branch` is `--branch`, `NGRACE_SPEC_BRANCH`, or `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`; it is refused when git is absent and no flag or env is given. The same inputs always produce the same id; the wall clock is never read. The resolved path is `.ngrace/changes/active/<ID>/spec.xml`.

**The refusal set, pinned — each writes nothing.** (a) a positional beginning `C-` is a hand-typed id: *"... is a hand-typed change id; pass the bare slug"*. (b) a slug whose final `-`-separated token is all digits is refused as ambiguous with lineage. (c) a positional already matching `ANCHOR_PATTERNS.mintedChange` is refused (the suffix is the tool's). (d) absent or invalid timestamp: *"spec new requires --timestamp or NGRACE_SPEC_TIMESTAMP"*. (e) unresolved branch: *"spec new requires --branch, NGRACE_SPEC_BRANCH, or a git working tree"*. (f) an unparseable `--supersedes` predecessor. (g) the resolved id already exists under `active/` or `archive/`: the shipped `refuseExistingBundle` message, which names the path. The `mint-search` success line reports the prior-slug counts, so the `Charter` can quote the tool's own collision half rather than restating a hand count.

**The lineage contract, pinned.** `parseBundleId(id)` returns `{ slug, lineage?, hash?, minted }`: minted ids (`ANCHOR_PATTERNS.mintedChange`) strip the trailing `-<HASH>` and then the `-<N>`, giving `slug`, `lineage`, `hash`, `minted=true`; a legacy id matching `ANCHOR_PATTERNS.change` with a trailing `-<[1-9][0-9]*>` gives that `lineage`, `minted=false`; any other legacy id gives `lineage=undefined`. The successor is `C-<same slug>-<(lineage ?? 1) + 1>-<HASH>`. Legacy `C-FOO` (no trailing digits) is read as lineage 1, so its successor is `C-FOO-2-<HASH>`; legacy `C-FOO-2` is lineage 2, so its successor is `C-FOO-3-<HASH>` — the legacy edge keeps the *old* names, never new hash-less ones. `supersede --replacement` accepts only the successor (same slug, next lineage), hash-less only when the directory already exists; when `--replacement` is omitted the verb mints the successor itself. `supersedeChangeBundle` is not otherwise changed: the mint happens in `src/grace-supersede.ts` before the call, and the shipped write and rollback order stays. The legacy-pair exception — accepting a fully hash-less different-slug replacement — was considered and rejected: it keeps open the hand path `D38` closes and leaves the successor's slug unconstrained.

`ngrace spec new <SLUG> --timestamp <ISO8601> --branch <name>` writes `.ngrace/changes/active/C-<SLUG>-1-<HASH>/spec.xml` whose wrapper tag equals its directory name, where `<HASH>` is exactly 8 uppercase hex characters, and prints the relative path on line 1 plus a `mint:` line naming the resolved id, slug, lineage, hash, branch and timestamp. `ngrace spec new --supersedes C-PRED …` resolves `<N>` to the predecessor's parsed lineage plus one and keeps the predecessor's slug. The instrument is production assertions over isolated temp roots in `src/grace-generate.test.ts`, the minted pattern and parser in `src/artifact/types.ts`. Red direction, driven on a copy: a template that emits a 7-character hash reddens the length clause; a `--supersedes` that copies the predecessor's `<N>` instead of incrementing reddens the lineage clause.

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-MINT-DETERMINISTIC:
The same `branch` and canonical timestamp always yield the same hash, and two different timestamps yield different hashes: driven by minting twice with identical inputs and diffing the wrapper tags, then minting with a second timestamp and asserting the ids differ. No wall clock is read — the instrument passes `--timestamp` explicitly, so a clock read would make two identical-input mints differ and redden the first clause. The instrument is production assertions in `src/grace-generate.test.ts`; the hash helper is exported and unit-tested against a hand-computed expected digest.
